items.body_md:
On August 31, Brandt Silverkorn of Edelson PC / Oppenheim + Zebrak filed a Transcript Designation Form (Dkt. 686) in the district court — the standard mechanism by which an appellant identifies, for the Ninth Circuit's record, which trial or hearing transcripts are to be prepared and transmitted as part of the appellate record. The filing is procedural, but in context it is worth flagging: it is the first concrete record-assembly step taken in either of the two pending fee appeals since the USCA Case Number entries (Dkts. 684–685) confirmed the Ninth Circuit had opened separate dockets for No. 26-5391 (Edelson PC / Oppenheim + Zebrak) and No. 26-5455 (Cowan DeBaets Abrahams & Sheppard LLP). 
No. 26-5391, filed August 18, appeals from the July 20 judgment (Dkt. 680) including all prior orders, with Edelson PC and Oppenheim + Zebrak intending to focus on the fee and expenses award.
 
No. 26-5455, filed August 19, also appeals from the July 20 judgment but is expressly limited to the district court's order granting in part the motion for attorneys' fees.
 The Transcript Designation Form was filed by Silverkorn — Edelson / O+Z counsel — which means Dkt. 686 is attributable to No. 26-5391; nothing on the district docket as of August 31 reflects a corresponding transcript designation from Cowan DeBaets.

The significance is limited but real. A transcript designation is procedural under FRAP 10(b) and Ninth Circuit Rule 10-3; it does not affect any party's legal rights or the class's recovery posture directly. It does, however, signal that Edelson / O+Z is actively prosecuting its appeal and has moved to the record-preparation phase. Cowan DeBaets' parallel absence from the district docket through August 31 leaves open whether that firm has filed its own designation directly on the Ninth Circuit docket (where it would not appear here) or has not yet done so; that distinction matters because a failure to timely designate transcripts can draw a Ninth Circuit clerk's default notice. Neither the district docket nor any available public source confirms the status of Cowan DeBaets' transcript designation. No party has moved for consolidation of the two appeals, and no consolidation order has appeared on the district court's docket.

The class's recovery posture is unchanged. Anthropic's payment obligations run independently of the fee appeals — no party has moved for a stay — and the $450 million first installment (Scheduled Payment 1) remains due September 25, 2026. The next concrete milestones are: (1) Anthropic's $450 million Scheduled Payment 1 on September 25; and (2) Ninth Circuit scheduling orders establishing opening-brief deadlines for Nos. 26-5391 and 26-5455, which the circuit clerk typically issues within the first weeks after a case opens and which will set the appellate briefing clock for both fee disputes.

items.body_md:
On August 25, the district court clerk docketed Dkt. 685 — a second USCA Case Number entry — confirming that the Ninth Circuit has opened at least one additional appellate proceeding arising from the fee appeals filed by Edelson PC / Oppenheim + Zebrak (Dkt. 682, August 18) and Cowan DeBaets Abrahams & Sheppard LLP (Dkt. 683, August 19). Dkt. 684, filed August 21, was the first such notation; the appearance of a second entry four days later strongly suggests the court assigned separate docket numbers to the two appeals rather than immediately consolidating them into a single track. That said, the specific Ninth Circuit case numbers remain unconfirmed from publicly available sources: 
CourtListener's district-court docket for 4:24-cv-05417 was last updated August 23, 2026, and its data is sourced from PACER and RECAP, which may not be current
 — meaning the appellate docket numbers have not yet propagated to any public aggregator this desk can verify. Confirmation will come once the Ninth Circuit clerk's entries appear on PACER or a public index. For analytical purposes, the operative fact is that two separate USCA Case Number notations now sit on the district docket, one per notice of appeal, consistent with the clerk opening two distinct appellate files.

The substantive posture of the fee dispute is unchanged. 
Two firms involved in generating the $1.5 billion copyright settlement appealed to the Ninth Circuit after being cut out of the $101 million attorney fee award, which was restricted to court-approved class counsel Susman Godfrey and Lieff Cabraser Heimann & Bernstein.
 
A week before he retired, Judge Alsup castigated plaintiffs' counsel for improperly requesting $75 million for work done by the two appealing firms and Cowan DeBaets in an initial $300 million fees request.
 Whether each appellant group is challenging only its exclusion from the fee award or also mounting a broader attack on the July 20 final approval order remains unconfirmed on the face of the notices; that question will be answered when opening briefs are filed. The existence of two separate appellate files — rather than a consolidated one — creates a procedural fork: the Ninth Circuit will need to decide, either sua sponte or on motion, whether to consolidate the proceedings. Consolidation is standard where appeals arise from the same underlying order and share common issues, but it is not automatic, and separate scheduling orders could issue in the interim.

For class members, Dkt. 685 closes the opening phase of the appellate record: both fee appellants now have active Ninth Circuit cases, the Effective Date has not arrived, and the disbursement portal remains dormant. Anthropic's payment obligations run independently of the appeals, and no party has moved for a stay. The $450 million first installment (Scheduled Payment 1) falls due September 25, 2026 — four weeks out. The next concrete milestones are: (1) the Ninth Circuit's scheduling orders establishing opening-brief deadlines for each docket, typically issued within weeks of case opening; and (2) any consolidation order, which would determine whether the two appeals proceed on a unified or parallel track and could affect both briefing timelines and the ultimate scope of any panel decision.

items.body_md:
On August 21, the clerk docketed Dkt. 684 — a USCA Case Number entry — confirming that the Ninth Circuit has accepted and assigned a docket number to at least one of the two pending fee appeals. The entry follows the notices filed by Edelson PC and Oppenheim + Zebrak (Dkt. 682, August 18) and Cowan DeBaets Abrahams & Sheppard LLP (Dkt. 683, August 19). The district court's notation of a USCA case number is the ministerial step that closes the opening of an appellate proceeding: the Ninth Circuit clerk has received the record, opened a case file, and issued a number that all subsequent appellate filings must reference. Whether the court assigned a single number to both appeals or opened two separate proceedings — and whether it has already or will sua sponte consolidate them — is not apparent from the face of Dkt. 684 alone and cannot be confirmed from available public sources this morning. The specific Ninth Circuit docket number(s) will become confirmable once the appellate docket appears on PACER or a public aggregator.

The substantive posture is unchanged but the procedural clock is now running at the appellate level. Once the Ninth Circuit issues its scheduling order — standard practice shortly after a case number is assigned — opening-brief deadlines will be set, typically running 40 days from the date the record on appeal is filed. 
The fee dispute at the core of both appeals centers on the district court's denial of class counsel's requested 12.5% fee (which would have yielded $187,500,000) and its substitution of a lodestar-multiplier award of $101,561,111 plus approximately $3 million in expense reimbursements
 — and, critically for the appellants, the exclusion of Edelson, Oppenheim + Zebrak, and Cowan DeBaets from any share of that award. Until opening briefs are filed, the precise legal theory each appellant group is pressing — fee exclusion only, or a broader challenge to the July 20 final approval order — remains unconfirmed on the face of the notices.

For class members, the assignment of a USCA case number is procedurally expected but consequential: it confirms the appellate track is live and the Effective Date has not arrived. The disbursement portal remains dormant, and the approximately 70% first-stage distribution stays in abeyance for the duration of the Ninth Circuit proceedings absent a court order or negotiated arrangement permitting earlier release of undisputed settlement funds. Anthropic's payment obligations run independently. 
The 30-day window from July 20 during which appeals could be noticed has now closed
, meaning the appellate record is set and no additional notices of appeal are expected. Anthropic's $450 million first installment (Scheduled Payment 1) falls due September 25, 2026 — that obligation is not stayed by the pending appeals, and no party has moved for a stay. The next concrete milestone is the Ninth Circuit's issuance of scheduling orders establishing opening-brief deadlines and formally resolving whether the two appeals proceed separately or on a consolidated track.

items.body_md:
On August 19, Cowan DeBaets Abrahams & Sheppard LLP filed its own notice of appeal to the Ninth Circuit (Dkt. 683), paying the $605 filing fee and entering the appeal alongside Edelson PC and Oppenheim + Zebrak, who had done the same the prior day (Dkt. 682). The two notices are separate filings by separate appellants, not a consolidated submission — meaning the Ninth Circuit will open at least two docketed appeal proceedings arising from the July 20 final approval order, though the court may consolidate them on motion or sua sponte. Both appellant groups were coordinating-counsel or fee-claimant firms rather than class counsel, and together they were the primary drivers of the approximately $75 million supplemental fee request that Anthropic opposed as lacking "scant justification or substantiation" and that Judge Martínez-Olguín resolved as part of the July 20 order setting aside roughly $101.5 million in attorney fees for class counsel. The back-to-back filings, one on each side of the August 19 appeal deadline, confirm the fee outcome rather than the settlement's substantive terms is the operative grievance — though until opening briefs are filed, the precise scope of each appeal remains unconfirmed on the face of the notices.

The structural consequence for class members is unchanged from yesterday but now fully locked: with two sets of appellants on the record, the Effective Date under the settlement agreement cannot arrive, the disbursement portal will not launch, and the roughly 70% first-stage distribution remains in abeyance for the duration of the Ninth Circuit proceedings. 
Payments were to be made in two stages, roughly 70% in the first stage and 30% in the second, as Anthropic will be making settlement payments in installments through September 2027.
 The critical distinction for recovery posture — whether the appeal is confined to fees or extends to final approval itself — will determine whether class members face a full stay of all disbursements or only a hold on funds attributable to disputed counsel compensation. If cabined to fees, there is a plausible argument that undisputed settlement funds could be released to class members during the pendency of the appeal, but that would require either a negotiated arrangement or a court order, neither of which appears on the docket. No stay motion has been filed by any party.

Anthropic's payment obligations run independently of the appeal absent a stay. 
Per the settlement's payment schedule, Anthropic's $450 million first installment (Scheduled Payment 1) falls due September 25, 2026.
 That obligation is not suspended by the filing of a notice of appeal, and no party has moved to stay the judgment. The practical question for the coming weeks is whether any party moves in the district court or the Ninth Circuit for a stay pending appeal, which would require the movant to demonstrate likelihood of success on the merits, irreparable harm, balance of equities, and public interest — a high bar for a fee dispute in a settled class action. The next concrete milestone is the Ninth Circuit's assignment of case numbers and issuance of scheduling orders for both appeals, which will establish the opening-brief deadlines and clarify whether the court consolidates the two proceedings.

items.body_md:
On August 18, Edelson PC and Oppenheim + Zebrak filed a notice of appeal to the Ninth Circuit (Dkt. 682), taking the final approval order entered July 20 up on appeal and triggering the precise scenario that has held class member payments in abeyance since that order issued.

The filing's immediate consequence is concrete: 
under the settlement agreement, payments begin one business day after the "Effective Date," defined as the date on which the time to file or notice an appeal of the final judgment expires
 — a date that was today, August 19. That condition is no longer satisfied. 
If an appeal is filed, according to class counsel, the claims process will be on pause temporarily until they can determine how to proceed.
 The end-of-August launch of the online disbursement portal 
that was contingent on no appeals being filed
 does not follow. 
Payments were to be made in two stages, roughly 70% in the first stage and 30% in the second, as Anthropic will be making settlement payments in installments through September 2027
 — a disbursement timeline that now runs on an uncertain clock pending the Ninth Circuit's disposition.

The identity of the appellants is material context. Edelson PC and Oppenheim + Zebrak were not class counsel; they served as coordinating counsel and were the center of a sustained fee dispute throughout the proceedings. 
The firms — along with Cowan DeBaets Abrahams & Sheppard — had jointly sought roughly $75 million in fees, and Anthropic urged the court to deny that request, arguing there was "scant justification or substantiation" for the request.
 
Judge Martínez-Olguín granted final approval on July 20 and set aside roughly $101.5 million in attorney fees for class counsel
 — well below the aggregate originally sought across all firms. The appeal, filed by counsel who contested the fee outcome, almost certainly targets that fee award, though the notice of appeal (Dkt. 682) does not specify grounds on its face. The filing of a standard notice — rather than a Rule 23(f) petition for permission to appeal — is consistent with an appeal of right from a final judgment, which the July 20 order constitutes. 
Judge Martínez-Olguín overruled all 53 objections filed with the court opposing the settlement on various grounds
, so class members who objected to settlement terms also had standing to appeal; the notice, however, identifies only Edelson and Oppenheim + Zebrak as appellants, pointing toward the fee dispute rather than the merits of the settlement itself.

For class members, the practical import is a delay of indeterminate length. Ninth Circuit appeals of class action final approval orders regularly take 12 to 24 months to resolve absent a settlement of the appeal or a motion to dismiss. The first Anthropic installment payment of $450 million remains calendared for September 25, 2026 — Anthropic's payment obligation under the settlement agreement is not suspended by the appeal absent a stay, and no stay motion appears on the docket as of this briefing. Whether the appeal extends to the settlement itself or is cabined to fees will be the threshold question once the opening brief is filed; that distinction drives whether class members face a full stay of disbursements or merely a hold on funds attributable to counsel fees. The next concrete docket event to watch is the Ninth Circuit's docketing of the appeal and any emergency motion practice around a stay.

items.body_md:
On August 7, the Textbook & Academic Authors Association published a summary of class counsel's confirmed guidance on payment timing, the first direct statement from counsel on the post-final-approval distribution timeline. 
Class counsel confirmed that class members will not begin receiving payments until at least the end of 2026.
 The gate is the August 19 appeal deadline: 
under the settlement agreement, payments begin one business day after the "Effective Date," defined as the date on which the time to appeal the final judgment expires, and the Ninth Circuit generally allows 30 days to appeal.
 
Payments could be further delayed if anyone files an appeal before that August 19 deadline.
 With nine days remaining in the appeal window, no appeal has been publicly reported or docketed; confirmation would require a notice of appeal appearing on the docket.


Payments will be made in two stages, roughly 70% in the first stage and 30% in the second, as Anthropic will be making settlement payments in installments through September 2027.
 That structure maps directly onto the funded installments: $600 million is already in the settlement fund (the October 2025 and April 2026 tranches), with the third installment of $450 million due September 25, 2026, and a fourth of $450 million due September 25, 2027, per the settlement agreement. 
If no appeals are filed, an online portal will be launched by end of August containing claimants' consolidated claim forms
 — a concrete operational step that would signal the distribution machinery is running. For claimants, the recovery posture is straightforward: the August 19 deadline is the single controlling variable between here and first payment; a clean passage through it puts initial disbursements on track for late 2026, while any appeal filed by a disgruntled class member or the Passman opt-out litigation restarts the clock.

The next concrete milestone is August 19 — the expiration of the 30-day appeal window from Judge Martínez-Olguín's July 20 final approval order (Dkt. 680). A clean passage triggers the "Effective Date" under the settlement agreement and, per class counsel's guidance, unlocks portal launch and first-wave distribution. The milestone after that is September 25, 2026: Anthropic's third installment payment of $450 million.

items.body_md:
The sole development in the 72-hour window is a class-counsel-sourced update published yesterday by the Textbook & Academic Authors Association. 
Class counsel confirmed that class members will not begin receiving payments until at least the end of 2026, with disbursement contingent on whether any appeals are filed before the August 19 deadline.
 That deadline — 11 days out — is now the controlling variable for the entire distribution timeline. 
Payments will be made in two stages, roughly 70% in the first stage and 30% in the second, reflecting Anthropic's installment payment structure running through September 2027.
 The practical implication is that even in the no-appeal scenario, claimants are looking at a partial recovery in late 2026 and a residual tail payment that tracks Anthropic's funding calendar, not a single lump disbursement.

The August 19 appeal deadline is the nearest binary event. 
If no appeals are filed, class counsel indicated that an online portal will be launched by the end of August containing claimants' consolidated claim forms
 — the administrative precursor to actual disbursement. Any timely appeal would halt that sequence and push payments into an indeterminate window governed by appellate scheduling. The identity and standing of a potential appellant remains the relevant uncertainty: 
Judge Martínez-Olguín overruled all 53 objections and recorded 350 valid opt-outs representing 1,802 works, or 0.03% of the total
 — a thin objector pool, though standing to appeal is not limited to those who formally objected at the trial-court level. The Passman late opt-out application (Dkt. 676), opposed by both class counsel (Dkt. 678) and Anthropic (Dkt. 679) and disposed of in the July 20 final approval order (Dkt. 680), is the most obvious candidate for appellate review, but whether Passman's counsel has filed or intends to file a notice of appeal is unconfirmed as of this writing; confirmation would require a notice of appeal appearing on the docket.

Today's update is procedural in character — a payment-timeline clarification from class counsel, not a docket filing or judicial action. It does not alter the recovery math or the settlement structure. The next concrete milestone is August 19: if the docket is clean at close of business that day, the portal launch and late-2026 first-stage disbursement become the operative working assumption. The subsequent hard date is September 25, 2026, when Anthropic's third installment payment is due, bringing the funded total to $1.05 billion of the $1.5 billion obligation.
